about: Living Roots Wine & Co. was founded in 2016 by Sebastian and Colleen Hardy and makes wine on two continents. Seb comes from six generations of South Australian winemakers, beginning with Thomas Hardy, who arrived in 1850 and planted some of the colony’s first vines; his father Geoff planted the first vineyard in Kuitpo, at the southern end of the Adelaide Hills. Colleen, from the Rochester area, met Seb while working a vintage there. Their Australian reds come from family-connected vineyards, and in 2023 Halliday’s Wine Companion named Living Roots Australia’s Best New Winery.

The Adelaide Hills are one of South Australia’s coolest regions, and their Shiraz is leaner and spicier than the full-throttle styles of the warm valleys below. Living Roots leans into that freshness. The grapes are destemmed but not crushed, keeping a high proportion of whole berries; half is fermented in open vats and punched down twice a day, and the other half is sealed for ten days of carbonic maceration, which lifts the fruit. All of it ferments on wild yeasts.

The winemakers describe a vibrant Shiraz with lifted dark fruit, fresh acidity, and spicy, savoury notes in balance: closer in spirit to a cool-climate Syrah than a classic blockbuster. Carbonic maceration, the technique associated with Beaujolais, starts fermentation inside unbroken berries, which gives juicy, perfumed fruit and softer tannins. Here it keeps a cool-climate Shiraz bright and lively.
facts: Whole berries; half open-fermented, half 10 days carbonic maceration (producer’s 2019 method)
